http://www.bing.com/news/apiclick.aspx?r.summary_en: The plague, a rare bacterial infection that killed tens of millions in 14th-century Europe, has not gone away. Since the 1990s, most human cases have been reported in Africa, especially Congo and Madagascar. In the U.S., there are an average of about seven human cases per year, mostly in rural areas of the American West. A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia recently died of pneumonia, raising concerns in Russia.
